prompt: some people argue that parents should have a strong influence on their children’s choice of friends and life partners. Others believe that young people should make these decisions independently. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
The importance of parents having a strong influence on their children’s choice of friends and life partners, which was always debatable, has now become more controversial, with many people claiming that it is beneficial while others reject this notion. The substantial influence of this trend has sparked controversy over its potential impact in recent years. In my opinion, the former proposition appears to be more rational. This essay will further elaborate on both views and thus lead to a logical conclusion.

There are myriad of  reasons which will further explain this argument, but the most preponderant one stems from the fact that parents have greater life experience and can guide their children towards suitable people. This is important because young individuals may sometimes make decisions based mainly on emotions without considering the long-term consequences. Another pivotal aspect of this argument is that parents generally understand their children's personality, family background, and future needs. Therefore, their advice can help young people avoid unhealthy friendships or relationships. Needless to say, all these merits stand in good stead.

However, there are some pitfalls that negate these arguments and which can certainly overwhelm the potential influence of this trend, but one of the most alarming ones is that excessive parental involvement may restrict the freedom of young people. They should be able to choose their own friends and life partners because these relationships directly affect their happiness. Moreover, making such decisions independently can help them develop confidence and decision-making skills. Hence, it is apparent why many are against strong parental control.

According to the arguments aforementioned above, one can reach the conclusion that the benefits of parental guidance are instrumental indeed. Nevertheless, parents should provide advice rather than completely control their children's decisions, and the final choice should ultimately belong to the young person.
